classifyPlanningChain(commands) -> {kind:"PROPOSE"} | {kind:"FINALIZE"} | {kind:"REFUSED", code:"PLANNING_FINALIZE_CHAIN_MIXED"} | {kind:"UNSUPPORTED"}. Reads the LAST element's kind through a descriptor-safe `own` read; if the chain also contains the OTHER terminal kind it is MIXED. UNSUPPORTED keeps the pre-existing BOOTSTRAP_PAYLOAD_INVALID behaviour for a chain ending in neither, so the widening is strictly additive.

callerSuppliedAuthorityBodies(payload, commands) scans BOTH caller-controlled surfaces — the request payload and every chain element — for a closed 5-key roster {acceptanceContract, authority, envelope, planRevision, sealedHashes}. `authority`/`envelope` are in the roster because the core reducer IGNORES unknown command members, so a smuggled one would otherwise ride into the decision's request bytes unexamined; `sealedHashes` because the run's hashes are the reducer's OUTPUT.

buildPlanningAuthorityEnvelopeLeg({request, runId, state, store}):
1. reads the durable record via store.readEvents(planningAuthorityAggregateId(runId)) filtered to eventType "PlanningAuthorityBodiesSealed"; no such event => {kind:"ABSENT"} (the legacy arm).
2. decodes BOTH bodies with core's decodePlanRevisionBytes / decodeAcceptanceContractBytes; refusals travel out with the CORE's own code and layer, never restated. A record whose bytes do not decode is deliberately NOT reported as absent: it degrades to an EMPTY record, whose missing body bytes are refused by the core body codec (decodePlanRevisionBytes takes `unknown` and answers PLAN_REVISION_BYTES_INVALID). A corrupt record can therefore never be laundered into "this run carried no authority".
3. composes the b42db644 envelope — acceptanceContract/planRevision from the DECODED durable bodies; bindings {goalRef: state.goalRef, projectId: request.projectId, revisionId: RECORD.revisionId, runId}; submission {criteriaDigest: RECORD.criteriaDigest, goalRef, graphRevisionRef, lifecycle, projectId, runId, sealedHashes, submissionHash} all from the JUST-FOLDED state; version = PLANNING_AUTHORITY_ENVELOPE_VERSION — and calls encodePlanningAuthorityEnvelope BEFORE any write. DESIGN NOTE: the two fields the RECORD contributes (revisionId, criteriaDigest) are exactly the two the codec cross-checks against the DECODED bodies (checks 4 and 9), so those checks are load-bearing here rather than comparing a value with itself. Every refusal returns {code, layer} verbatim from whichever of the three vocabularies answered.
4. on ok returns leg {aggregateId: planning-authority/<runId>, expectedVersion: store.getAggregateVersion(aggregateId) — NOT versionOf(ledger,...), which reads 0 forever for a secondary leg — events: [one "PlanningAuthorityEnvelopeSealed" draft, eventId `${runId}-PlanningAuthorityEnvelopeSealed`, payload {criteriaDigest, envelopeBytesBase64, envelopeDigest, planHash, projectId, runId}]} plus binding {authorityRef, envelopeDigest = sha256 over the canonical envelope bytes}.
